summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with a history of endometriosis was admitted for acute-on-chronic left lower quadrant pelvic pain radiating to the rectum and leg. Initial evaluation revealed stable vital signs after pain control, normal white blood cell count, negative pregnancy test, and a normal pelvic ultrasound with no evidence of torsion or free fluid. Pain was managed with intravenous and oral analgesics, including Dilaudid, tramadol, gabapentin, ibuprofen, and acetaminophen. Given the absence of infectious or structural causes, the pain was attributed to an endometriosis flare. She improved clinically and was discharged home on hospital day two with a regimen of oral pain medications and follow-up instructions.
